correctness.rationale: Every fPO allocation must assign type-(1,0) to cost-zero agent2 and type-(0,1) to cost-zero agent1, and any such allocation reaches minimum possible aggregate cost c. Shared assignment count x satisfies WEF precisely pc-qb<=x<=p(c+a). If a>0, agent2 necessarily holds a zero-cost chore; strong WEFX upon its removal enforces the lower bound in every lottery support, while ex-ante upper bound on E[x] ensures at least one support allocation meets upper bound; reverse for b>0. Hence point mass iff, and independent binomial choices yield 2^d sum C(c,x). Independent exhaustive small cases with a+b>=1, total chores≤6 and rational weights confirm criterion and count (728 cases); proof handles all nonnegative counts and p∈(0,1).
